traded lower in the premarket on Wednesday after its subsidiary Immunovant
failed in a proof-of-concept trial for IMVT-1402, an experimental therapy for a skin-related autoimmune condition known as cutaneous lupus erythematosus.

Citing 12-week data, the company said that the 57-patient trial did not achieve its primary endpoint, which was based on a clinical tool called the Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus Disease Area and Severity Index Activity (CLASI-A) score.

While results for the primary endpoint lacked statistical significance, multiple endpoints favored IMVT-1402 over placebo numerically, and the experimental therapy was found to have a promising safety and tolerability profile consistent with its prior studies, according to Roivant
Given rivalry in the CLE space and the trial results, Immunovant
no longer plans to advance IMVT-1402

title: Roivant slips as Immunovant faces trial setback for cutaneous lupus therapy
